title: The Perceived Effects of Using ChatGPT on Academic Writing Performance Among Senior High School Students
extended_summary:
This paper examines how senior high school students perceive the effects of using ChatGPT on their academic writing performance. The study is motivated by growing use of generative AI in education and by concern over both its potential benefits for writing support and its possible risks for originality, integrity, and overreliance. Rather than testing writing gains experimentally, the paper focuses on students’ reported experiences and perceived usefulness of ChatGPT for writing-related tasks.

The authors used a qualitative-descriptive survey approach with a paper-based open-ended questionnaire. Responses were analyzed thematically. The intervention was not a structured researcher-delivered program; instead, the study investigated students’ existing use of ChatGPT as a writing support tool. Reported uses included information gathering, idea generation, organization, grammar support, clarification of difficult topics, and vocabulary development.

The population consisted of Grade 12 Humanities and Social Sciences (HUMSS) students, indicating a senior high school sample in the Philippine context. The paper reports percentages of themes emerging from student responses: 45.35% viewed ChatGPT as effective for information gathering and idea generation, 25.58% associated it with improved productivity and task organization, 15.12% said it improved understanding of topics, and 13.95% perceived vocabulary benefits. The study appears to be based on one school context, though the exact school name and sample size are not reported in the provided text.

The main conclusion is that students generally perceive ChatGPT as a useful support tool for academic writing, particularly for generating ideas, organizing work, understanding content, and refining language. At the same time, the paper stresses that AI use should be balanced with independent thinking and ethical responsibility to preserve originality and academic integrity. The study contributes perception-based evidence rather than objective writing-quality outcomes.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative-descriptive survey using open-ended paper-based questionnaires and thematic analysis, with no experimental comparison, no validated performance assessment, and no reported reliability or psychometric evidence. It provides descriptive perception data but only limited causal credibility under the K-12 evidence framework.
impact_tier_rationale: The study suggests positive but unclear impact because outcomes are based on students' perceptions rather than independent writing assessments or extractable effect sizes. Reported percentages indicate perceived usefulness, but the magnitude of actual academic impact cannot be established.

interventions.use_case: Students used ChatGPT as a writing support tool for academic writing tasks, especially for idea generation, information gathering, grammar/language refinement, organization, vocabulary support, and topic explanation.
ChatGPT was also treated as a conversational AI resource that answered questions, explained confusing concepts, and provided examples/explanations to support students' writing-related understanding.

finding.finding_summary: This qualitative-descriptive survey reports positive perceived effects of ChatGPT on students' academic writing performance, particularly through idea generation, grammar support, organization, and vocabulary development. However, no direct writing-score gains, rubric-based essay scores, independent posttests, or causal effect sizes were reported; findings are perception-based percentages only, including 45.35% citing information gathering, 13.95% vocabulary development, and qualitative comments about grammatical correctness and better organization.
finding.measure: Open-ended questionnaire responses about perceived effects on academic writing performance

finding.finding_summary: Students perceived ChatGPT as supporting idea generation, understanding confusing questions, and improving comprehension of topics, suggesting perceived benefits for thinking through writing tasks and managing complex information. Still, these were self-reported perceptions from thematic analysis rather than validated measures of critical thinking, metacognition, or other durable skills, and no effect sizes were reported.
finding.measure: Open-ended perceptions related to idea generation, comprehension, and understanding of topics

finding.finding_summary: Approximately 25.58% of respondents reported that ChatGPT improved productivity by helping them organize ideas, manage time, generate drafts, and complete tasks more quickly. This indicates perceived efficiency gains in completing school writing tasks, but the study did not include objective productivity metrics, comparison groups, or extractable inferential statistics.
finding.measure: Open-ended questionnaire responses coded for productivity/task efficiency perceptions
